On servant of the Lord, see on <reference osisRef="Ps.18.1">Psa 18:1</reference>, title. The wickedness of man contrasted with the excellency of God's perfections and dispensations; and the benefit of the latter sought, and the evils of the former deprecated.</title> <div sID="gen8925" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5864"/>1. The general sense of this difficult verse is, "that the wicked have no fear of God." The first clause may be rendered, "Saith transgression in my heart, in respect to the wicked, there is no fear," &c., that is, such is my reflection on men's transgressions. <div eID="gen8925" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5865"/><div sID="gen8926" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5865"/>2-4. This reflection detailed.<div eID="gen8926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8927" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">until his iniquity--</hi>literally, "for finding his iniquity for hating"; that is, he persuades himself God will not so find it--"for hating" involving the idea of punishing. Hence his words of iniquity and deceit, and his bold rejection of all right principles of conduct. The climax is that he deliberately adopts and patronizes evil. The negative forms affirm more emphatically their contraries. <div eID="gen8927" type="x-p"/>
